The appellant being the accused in Special Case (POCSO) No.30/2021, on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge and FTSC-I (POCSO),
Kalaburagi (for short 'Trial Court'), is impugning the judgment of conviction dated 23.03.2023 and order of sentence dated 28.03.2023, convicting him for the offences punishable under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO') and under Section NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR 366A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and sentencing him:
(i) To undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 20 years for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and to pay fine of Rs.20,000/-;
(ii) To undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 366A of IPC with default sentences.

sentences.text:
The Trial Court has awarded Rs.7,00,000/- as compensation to the victim girl - PW.1.
2.

The case of the prosecution in brief is that, on 15.03.2021 at 9:00 a.m., when PW.1, the minor girl aged five years, was playing in front of the newly constructed Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Hostel, situated at Rajapur Road, Kalaburagi, the accused procured her with an intention to commit rape and Anand vs The State Through And Anr on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125214622/
2 committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault.

sentences.text:
Thereby committed the offence punishable NC:
2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR and under Sections 366A and 376(3) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
3. On registration of the FIR, on the basis of the first information lodged by PW.2, who is the mother of the victim girl, the investigation was undertaken and charge sheet came to be filed.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offences and registered the special case.
The accused appeared before the Trial Court and pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
4. The prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused, examined PW.1 to PW.16 and got marked Exs.P1 to P24 in support of its contention.
The accused has denied all the incriminatory materials available on record, but has not led any evidence in support of his defence.

The Trial Court after taking into consideration all these materials on record came to the conclusion that the prosecution is successful in proving the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts for the offences NC:
2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR punishable under Sections 366A and 376(3) of IPC and under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act.
Accordingly, he was convicted and sentenced as stated above.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant/accused is before this Court.
5. Heard learned counsel Sri Nandkishore Boob appearing for the appellant/accused and Sri Gopalkrishna B. Yadav, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State.
Perused the materials on record, including the Trial Court records.

6. In view of the contentions urged by learned counsel for the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court suffers from infirmities and calls for interference by this Court?"
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR

My answer to the above point is 'Partly in the Affirmative', for the following:
REASONS 7.
It is the contention of the prosecution that PW.1 - victim girl is aged five years, who is the daughter of the informant - PW.2.

When the victim girl was playing in front of Dr.B.R.Ambedkar Hostel at Rajapur Road, Kalaburagi, the accused had kidnapped the victim girl with an intention to commit sexual act and he has committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on her.
8. To prove this contention, the victim is examined as PW.1.
This witness being child, aged five years, has deposed before the Court in a manner stating that, she was subjected to sexual act.

sentences.text: PW.2 is the informant, who is the mother of the victim girl.
She states that her daughter was missing from the house and she was found weeping while coming out from the shed of the accused.
On enquiry, she stated NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR that, she was subjected to sexual act by the accused.
She deposed about filing of the complaint and subjecting the victim girl for medical examination.
This witness was cross-
examined at length, but nothing has been elicited to disbelieve her version.
10. PW.3 and PW.4 are the sisters of PW.2.
They have also supported the case of the prosecution.

Since the victim is aged five years, the evidence of PW.15 - the Doctor, who examined the victim girl,
plays an important role in depreciating the materials on record.
This witness states that, the victim girl was produced before her on 15.03.2021, with the history of sexual assault committed on her on 14.03.2021.
She examined the victim girl and issued certificate as per Ex.P18, received RFSL report as per Ex.P19 and gave her final opinion as per Ex.P20.
This witness was also subjected to cross-examination by the learned counsel for the accused, but nothing has been elicited to disbelieve her version.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR 11.
Ex.P18 is the medical report about sexual violence, but no opinion was expressed by the Medical Officer.
It is stated that supplementary report will follow after receiving the investigation report.
It is also found that the final opinion was kept pending for RFSL report.
Ex.P19 is the RFSL report.
According to which no seminal stains or spermatozoa were detected in any of the articles that were sent for examination.
Ex.P20 is the final opinion given by PW.15 to the effect that there is no evidence of recent sexual act committed on the victim girl.
If at all the accused has committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the victim aged 5 years, definitely PW-15 would have found signs of recent sexual act.
It is pertinent to note that, the incident had occurred on 14.03.2021 and the victim was subjected to examination on 15.03.2021.
Even then, there is specific opinion expressed by the Medical Officer that there was no evidence of recent sexual assault.

Under such circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prosecution is not successful in proving the guilt NC:
2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR of the accused either for Section 376(3) of IPC or Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act.

12. On perusal of the materials on record, including the evidence of the victim - PW-1, the medical report - Ex.P-18 and the evidence of PW-15, I am of the opinion that the prosecution is successful in proving the guilt of the accused for the offence under Section 7 punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

13. It is the contention of the prosecution that the accused has committed the offence punishable under Section 366(A) of IPC which refers to procuration of the minor girl by inducing her with an intention or knowledge that she will be forced to illicit intercourse with another person.
The said provision cannot be attracted in the present case.
Therefore, the prosecution is not successful in proving the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under Section 366(A) of IPC.

4 - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR liable for conviction only under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.
14.

sentences.text: I have gone through the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court.
It has proceeded to convict the accused for the offences punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 366(A) of IPC and sentenced him as stated above.
I do not find any justification for the Trial Court to pass the judgment of conviction for the aforesaid offences ignoring the medical evidence of PW-15 and documents Exs.P-18, P-19 and P-20.

Therefore, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment of conviction for the offences punishable under Sections 366A of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act is liable to be set aside but the accused is liable for conviction for the offence under Section 7 punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

Accordingly, I answer the above point 'partly in the affirmative' and proceed to pass the following:
- 11 -  NC: 2025:KHC-K:4495 HC-KAR  ORDER  (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment of conviction dated 23.03.2023 and order of sentence dated 28.03.2023 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge and FTSC-I (POCSO), Kalaburagi is hereby set aside.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (iii) Accused is convicted for the offence under Section 7 punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

(iv) He is sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of four years and is liable to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/- [Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only], in default of payment of fine, he shall undergo further imprisonment for a period of one year.
(v) The accused is entitled for set off for the period which he has already undergone.
(vi) The order regarding compensation to the victim girl is sustained.
